chunks: 5377 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Talhah ibn Zayd, from al-Fadl ibn Uthman, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who is killed, then his head is found in one tribe, his middle, chest, and hands in another tribe, and the remainder in another tribe, he عليه السلام said: "His diyah is upon the one in whose tribe his chest and hands are found, and the salat (funeral prayer) is upon him."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ عَلَيْهِ: The funeral prayer is to be performed over him
key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: His blood money or legal compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.صَدْرُهُ وَيَدَاهُ: His chest and hands, identified here as the determining body parts for legal responsibility
key_terms.قَبِيلَةٍ: A tribe or tribal jurisdiction in which the body parts are found

ai.seo_question: Which tribe is responsible for the diyah when a murdered body is found divided across different tribes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a murdered person whose body is found dismembered across different tribal territories. Imam Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام rules that liability for the diyah falls upon the tribe in whose area the chest and hands are found, and that the funeral prayer is performed over him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5377 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Al-Fadl ibn Uthman, who narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a man who was killed, and his head was found in one tribe, his torso and arms in another tribe, and the rest of his body in yet another tribe.
Imam (as) said: "The blood money is upon the tribe where his torso and arms were found, and the funeral prayer is to be performed over him."
